title: AI Technical Manager
description:
**Join our Team**
**About this opportunity:**
Join our team at Ericsson as a AI Technical Manager, a critical role that drives our end-to-end technical solutions based on customer specifications and burgeoning business needs. As part of our dynamic team, you will facilitate profitable business growth by bridging customer needs and technical opportunities into robust offerings and proposals. You will support the Consultants during the requirement analysis and high-level design phases while having the chance to assume responsibilities in Customer Support, sales, and service delivery.
  
  
**What you will do:**

* Lead end-to-end delivery of AI/ML and GenAI projects & ensuring alignment with business strategy and technical excellence.
* Manage cross-functional teams including AI engineers, data scientists, Python/Frontend developers, and solution architects.
* Translate complex business problems into scalable AI solutions and actionable roadmaps.
* Drive project estimation, resource planning, and cost modeling for AI initiatives; manage budgets and track ROI of AI programs.
* Oversee development and deployment of ML/GenAI models, APIs, and agentic systems ensuring reliability, compliance, and security.
* Define technical standards, reusable frameworks, and best practices for model lifecycle management (MLOps).
* Evaluate and select suitable LLMs, vector databases, and orchestration frameworks based on cost, scalability, and business impact.
* Collaborate with product owners, architects, and business stakeholders to prioritize and deliver high-value AI initiatives.
* Drive technical evaluations and integration of LLMs, vector databases, orchestration tools, and emerging GenAI frameworks.
* Mentor and guide team members on AI/ML concepts, design patterns, and responsible AI practices.
* Ensure timely delivery, risk management, and continuous improvement through agile project execution.

**The skills you bring:**

* Bachelor’s/Master’s degree in Computer Science, Engineering, Data Science, or related field.
* 10+ years of software development experience with at least 4+ years in AI/ML or GenAI solution delivery.
* Strong technical leadership and people management skills with proven delivery of enterprise-scale AI projects.
* Proficiency in Python (3.x), and hands-on understanding of ML/DL frameworks (PyTorch, TensorFlow, Hugging Face).
* Experience in architecting or managing GenAI systems using RAG pipelines, embeddings, and vector databases (Elastic, Pinecone, Milvus).
* Working knowledge of GenAI frameworks such as LangChain, LlamaIndex, LangGraph, AutoGen, and Crew.ai.
* Familiarity with MLOps pipelines (CI/CD for ML, monitoring, retraining, drift detection) and container orchestration (Docker/Kubernetes).
* Exposure to cloud AI platforms (Azure OpenAI, AWS Bedrock, GCP Vertex AI) and modern data architectures.
* Deep understanding of Responsible AI, governance, and compliance requirements in enterprise environments.
* Excellent communication and stakeholder management skills, with ability to bridge technical and business teams.
* Prior exposure to Telecom, BFSI, or large enterprise AI adoption programs.
* Certifications in AI/ML, Cloud (Azure/AWS), or Project Management (PMP, Agile).

**Why join Ericsson?**
At Ericsson, you´ll have an outstanding opportunity. The chance to use your skills and imagination to push the boundaries of what´s possible. To build solutions never seen before to some of the world’s toughest problems. You´ll be challenged, but you won’t be alone. You´ll be joining a team of diverse innovators, all driven to go beyond the status quo to craft what comes next.

We truly believe that by collaborating with people with different experiences we drive innovation, which is essential for our future growth. We encourage people from all backgrounds to apply and realize their full potential as part of our Ericsson team. Ericsson is proud to be an Equal Opportunity Employer. learn more.

To program manage the delivery, scaling and adoption of enterprise AI intelligence products that can translate business requirements into trusted insights and actionable recommendations for business leaders. The role bridges stakeholders, product, data, analytics, and technology teams to define use cases, align roadmaps, implement features, and ensure the products create measurable business impact.
  
  
**Key Tasks And Accountabilities**

* Own end-to-end program management for conversational AI intelligence products, from intake and prioritization through delivery, launch, adoption, and performance tracking.
* Lead a high performance team to advance on the strategy of build, buy and integrate agents to build world class AI intelligence products
* Partner with business stakeholders to capture requirements, clarify success metrics, translate needs into product-ready user stories, and manage trade-offs across scope, timing, and impact.
* Collaborate closely with product managers, data scientists, data engineers, UX, analytics, and technology teams to implement features that are accurate, usable, secure, and scalable.
* Build and maintain delivery roadmaps, sprint/release plans, dependency maps, risk logs, decision records, and executive-ready status reporting.
* Drive adoption of AI products through stakeholder enablement, launch communications, training materials, feedback loops, and operating routines.
* Define and monitor product health metrics, including usage, answer quality, adoption, business value, model/data quality issues, and stakeholder satisfaction.
* Establish governance routines for responsible AI delivery, including data readiness, privacy, access controls, human-in-the-loop review, quality assurance, and escalation paths.
* Identify high-value use cases, evaluate feasibility with product and data teams, and sequence delivery to maximize business impact while managing complexity.
* Serve as the operating bridge between business, product, data, and technology teams, removing blockers and ensuring decisions are made at the right level.
* Support alignment between local, zone, and global AI strategies so conversational AI products can be reused, scaled, and continuously improved.
* BUSINESS ENVIRONMENT

**Main Characteristics:**
This role operates in a fast-moving AI product environment where business teams need practical intelligence products that improve decision-making, automate insight access, and create repeatable ways of working. The role requires strong program discipline, stakeholder management, product fluency, and enough technical understanding to partner effectively with data and engineering teams.
  
  
Geographical Scope: Global / Zone scope depending on product portfolio and deployment roadmap.
  
  
**Key Dimensions and Contacts:**
Business stakeholders and functional leaders who sponsor use cases and define adoption needs.
  
  
Product leaders and product managers responsible for roadmap, prioritization, user experience, and release planning.
  
  
Data science, data engineering, analytics engineering, platform, architecture, security, and privacy teams responsible for implementation and governance.
  
  
Analytics, insights, commercial, revenue management, marketing, operations, and transformation teams as end users and adoption partners.
  
  
External technology or implementation partners where needed to accelerate delivery while protecting product ownership and avoiding vendor lock-in.
  
  
**Qualifications, Experience, Skills**
Please list the following requirements
  
  
**Level of educational attainment required:**

* BS degree in Engineering, Computer Science, Data/Analytics, Business, or related field. MBA, Masters degree, product management certification, or agile/program management certification preferred.

**Previous work experience required:**

* 6+ years of relevant business, product, analytics, technology, or consulting experience, including experience managing cross-functional delivery programs. Experience with AI, GenAI, conversational products, analytics products, data platforms, or digital transformation strongly preferred. CPG or enterprise-scale technology experience is a plus.

**Language skills required:**

* English required; Spanish and/or Portuguese preferred depending on location

**IT skills required:**

* Strong understanding of product delivery, agile ways of working, analytics/data products, conversational AI concepts, prompt and response-quality evaluation, data pipelines, dashboards, user acceptance testing, release management, and adoption tracking. Ability to work with product, data science, data engineering, UX, architecture, security, and privacy teams without needing to be the technical implementer.

**Other skills required:**

* Program management: delivery planning, risk and dependency management, stakeholder alignment, executive communication, prioritization, and change control.
* Business analysis: ability to translate ambiguous business needs into requirements, user journeys, acceptance criteria, success metrics, and product backlog items.
* Product mindset: customer empathy, adoption focus, iterative delivery, value measurement, and continuous improvement.
* AI delivery discipline: understanding of responsible AI practices, data readiness, answer-quality evaluation, human review, governance, and model/product performance monitoring.
* Communication: exceptional written, verbal, and presentation skills, with the ability to explain technical topics clearly to business audiences and business trade-offs clearly to technical teams.
* Collaboration: strong relationship-building, influencing, negotiation, and facilitation skills across senior stakeholders and execution teams.
* Operating style: comfortable with ambiguity, able to create structure quickly, and resilient in a dynamic environment with evolving AI capabilities and business priorities.

* Ability to collaborate effectively and bridge the gap between business needs and technology solutions.
* A strategic problem‑solver who challenges assumptions and recommends innovative, future‑ready approaches.
* A committed team player focused on delivering value, driving transformation, and building lasting client relationships

* Approximately 5 to 10 years of experience working in Life & Annuity insurance domain.

* Hands‑on experience with policy lifecycle processes and insurance operational workflows.
* Ability to produce high‑quality process maps, data flows, and requirement documentation.
* Proficiency in managing multi‑vendor engagements and navigating complex project environments.
* Analytical mindset with the ability to interpret data, identify gaps, and propose practical solutions.
* Excellent communication and facilitation skills for client‑facing interactions.
* Ability to collaborate effectively with technical, functional, and business stakeholders.

**Ideally, good to have**

* Experience working on data migration projects and applying data governance best practices.
* Knowledge of insurance COTS platforms such as FAST, ALIP, OIPA, wmA etc

* Understanding of upstream and downstream integrations across the policy lifecycle
* Knowledge of project management tools like JIRA, TFS, Azure DevOps

title: Head Channel Strategy
description:
**SRMB STEEL \| JOB DESCRIPTION** 




**Head of Channel Strategy** 




*Owner of secondary \& tertiary counter billing strategy, counter share and reach* 




**Position** 




 Channel Strategy Head
 



**Function** 




 Sales and Marketing, Channel Strategy
 



**Grade / Level** 




 Assistant Vice President (AVP)
 



**Reports to** 




 President and Chief Sales \& Marketing Officer
 



**Directly leads** 




 Lead, Counter Share and Lead, Reach
 



**Location** 




 Kolkata head office with field travel
 



**Experience** 




 12 years and above in building materials retail channel strategy
 



  





**1\. Why this role exists** 




 SRMB tracks its business through primary billing to the depot or distributor and secondary movement to the dealer. What it does not track is tertiary: the actual sell\-out at the root retail counter to the mason, contractor and home builder. That is the single largest blind spot in the commercial engine. When the counter sale is invisible, demand planning runs on stale proxies, counter potential stays unmapped, and share is lost one counter at a time without anyone seeing it happen.
 



 This role fixes that. The Channel Strategy Head makes root counter billing a measured, managed number, then uses it to drive two outcomes at once: a deeper share of each counter we already serve, and a wider presence in the counters we should serve but do not. Digital is the thread that stitches these efforts together for maximum reach at the lowest cost to serve.
 



  





**2\. The mandate** 




**Three jobs sit under one leader.** 



* **Root counter billing efficacy.** 
 Stand up tertiary tracking as a first\-class metric. Define what a tracked counter looks like, roll out the capture discipline through the field and the DMS, and turn counter billing into the number the zone reviews every week, not an afterthought behind primary and secondary.
* **Lead Counter Share.** 
 Grow SRMB's wallet share at every active counter through range selling across TMT, WINGRIP, the binding range and Real\-Edge, better counter productivity, and the recovery of dormant counters. Own the counter share pod.
* **Lead Reach.** 
 Expand numeric reach into high\-potential counters where SRMB is absent, guided by a live potential map, and use digital demand capture to pull those counters open. Own the reach pod.



  





**3\. Key responsibilities** 



* **Build the tertiary layer.** 
 Design and institutionalize root counter billing tracking so tertiary offtake is captured, trusted and acted on at counter, town, district and zone level.
* **Map counter potential.** 
 Build and maintain a district\-level potential map of where SRMB should be present: counter universe, category demand, competitor hold and white space, so reach decisions are made on data, not on habit.
* **Own demand planning at the edge.** 
 Convert tertiary signals into counter and district level demand forecasts that feed production, stocking and dispatch, and raise forecast accuracy season on season.
* **Stitch the digital effort.** 
 Bring DMS, field force automation, geo\-tagging, influencer and loyalty programs and demand\-generation martech into one connected flow, so counter data, offtake and reach campaigns reinforce each other for maximum reach.
* **Drive counter share and range selling.** 
 Set and chase share\-of\-counter targets, lift lines billed per counter, and shrink the dormant\-counter base.
* **Lead and build two pods.** 
 Recruit, coach and hold accountable the Counter Share and Reach teams, and set the cadence of counter reviews with zonal and area teams.



  





**4\. Key result areas** 




**Result area** 




**How success is measured** 




  





**Tertiary visibility** 




 Share of active counters with tracked, trusted root billing; from near zero today to the agreed coverage target
 



**Counter share** 




 SRMB wallet share per counter and lines billed per counter (range selling index)
 



**Reach** 




 Numeric reach, new counter additions and white\-space closure against the potential map
 



**Demand planning** 




 Counter and district level forecast accuracy, and reduction in stock\-outs and dead inventory
 



**Digital adoption** 




 Active DMS and field\-force usage, share of counters geo\-tagged and digitally billed
 



**Counter productivity** 




 Revenue per active counter and reduction in the dormant\-counter base
 



  





**5\. Who we are looking for** 



* 12 years and above in retail channel strategy in the building materials industry: steel, cement, paints, tiles, pipes or construction chemicals. A minimum of 10 to 12 years is non\-negotiable.
* Proven command of primary, secondary and, above all, tertiary sales, with hands\-on experience making counter sell\-out a tracked number.
* Strong demand planning credentials, from field signal to forecast to stocking decision.
* A track record of counter potential mapping and white\-space expansion across multi\-district geographies.
* Practical experience rolling out DMS, field force automation and digital demand generation, and getting the field to actually use them.
* MBA or equivalent preferred. Comfort with data and dashboards is expected, not optional. Willing to spend real time in the field where counters live.



  





**6\. What good looks like in year one** 




 Root counter billing is a live, reviewed number across priority zones. The potential map is built and reach is expanding against it, not against gut feel. Demand planning is running off tertiary signal, and the two pods are staffed, capable and hitting counter share and reach targets. Digital tools are adopted in the field, not sitting idle. In short, the counter stops being a blind spot and becomes SRMB's sharpest source of growth.

This role bridges business, actuarial, and technical teams to ensure accurate, compliant, and auditable migration of in\-force policy data, values, and transaction history from source to target systems.

**Conversion Strategy \& Governance**
* Define the end\-to\-end conversion approach: crosswalk methodology, data mapping standards, tolerance thresholds, and reconciliation framework between legacy and target platforms.

**Business \& Technical Bridge**
* Translate legacy policy administration rules (billing, values, riders, beneficiaries, agent/commission structures) into target system configuration requirements.

**Data Mapping \& Rules Definition**
* Author functional specifications for field\-level, transaction\-level, and history conversion (policy, billing, claims\-in\-progress, agent/commission, correspondence).

**Testing \& Reconciliation**

**Team \& Stakeholder Management**

title: Head of Technology and Operational Efficiency
description:
**About the role** 




 iLEAD runs 19 undergraduate and postgraduate programmes across business, media, animation, IT and allied health sciences. As the institution has grown, so has the number of software systems, tools and manual processes in daily use across departments. Several of these are underused, poorly integrated, or worked around rather than worked with. This role exists to change that. The person we are looking for will take ownership of how technology is chosen, implemented and actually used across iLEAD, and will work with each department to find where better use of technology and clearer measurement can improve output and reduce cost. This is not a software\-building role. It is a role about making the systems we have, and the ones we adopt next, deliver real value in the hands of the people who use them.
 



 It is important to be clear about the balance of this work. The technical side matters, but it is the smaller part. The larger and harder part is getting people across a busy institution to adopt new systems and new ways of working, and to keep using them after the novelty fades. As a rough guide, expect around two thirds of the role to be people, change and coordination across departments, and about one third to be technical. The right person is comfortable with both, and is drawn to the harder two thirds rather than hiding in the easier one third.
 



**What you will own** 




**ERP rollout, adoption and maintenance** 



* Take end\-to\-end ownership of the institution\&\#39;s ERP: implementation, integration, maintenance, rollout, and day\-to\-day usage across departments.
* Resolve outstanding integration gaps so that data flows cleanly between systems instead of being re\-entered by hand, working with the relevant departments to agree the workflows that make this possible.
* Bring the institution's core administrative processes onto the system in a way that is accurate, trackable and reliable, so that leadership has a dependable picture of operations and finances.
* Make sure departments use the ERP as intended, not partially or reluctantly, and hold the standard once it is set.



**Communication and collaboration platforms** 



* Introduce, roll out and embed communication and collaboration platforms across the organisation.
* Design the adoption plan, run the training, and follow up until the new way of working has replaced the old one in practice, not just on paper.



**KPI and KRA implementation** 



* Build and own a KPI and KRA framework, and roll it out across departments so that each function has clear, measurable outcomes.
* Work with department heads to understand what each team actually does day to day, and turn that into a shared, visible picture that closes the gap between departments and leadership.
* Provide leadership with clear reporting on how the organisation is performing at the department and institution level, so that decisions rest on evidence rather than impression.



**Efficiency and Cost** 



* Work department by department to understand how work gets done today and where technology and better process can improve output, remove duplicated effort, and reduce cost.
* Review the software, tools and subscriptions the institution pays for, identify what is unused or overlapping, and consolidate where it makes sense.
* Bring findings to leadership with clear numbers and a practical plan, including the difficult findings, presented with judgement and discretion.



**Technology Direction** 



* Advise leadership on which tools and platforms iLEAD should invest in, extend, or retire, with a clear read on cost versus value.
* Identify where AI\-enabled tools can genuinely improve efficiency in administrative and support functions, and introduce them where they earn their place. AI is one tool among several here, not the purpose of the role.
* Set basic standards for data quality, access and security across the systems in use.



**What we are looking for** 




**Essential** 



* Experience owning or driving the implementation, rollout and adoption of business systems such as ERP, and getting non\-technical teams to use them properly.
* A track record of change management: introducing new tools, systems or measurement across an organisation and making the change stick against resistance.
* Experience defining and rolling out performance measurement such as KPIs or KRAs across multiple teams.
* The standing and maturity to work with senior, long\-serving colleagues, and to be firm and diplomatic at the same time, including when the message is not one people want to hear.
* A strong understanding of how technology, data and process connect, with enough technical depth to hold vendors and internal teams to account.
* Comfort with data: able to build or direct the reporting that shows leadership where effort and money are going.
* Clear, concise written and spoken communication, and the confidence to present uncomfortable findings to leadership.



**Desirable** 



* Experience in a multi\-department, service\-oriented organisation, and exposure to the education sector.
* Hands\-on experience with AI\-enabled tools and workflows in an operational setting.
* Experience with software licensing or cost and subscription rationalisation.
* Familiarity with common ERP suites, collaboration platforms, and modern data and reporting tools.



**What success looks like in the first year** 




 These are deliberately practical targets for the first twelve months. The value of this role compounds over time as adoption deepens.
 


* **Months 1 to 3:** 
 A clear picture of the systems, tools and processes in use across iLEAD, what they cost, and where they are underused or duplicated.
* **Months 3 to 6:** 
 ERP integration gaps closed and a working adoption plan in place for the departments not yet using it as intended, with core administrative and financial processes moving onto the system.
* **Months 6 to 9:** 
 Communication platform rolled out and in regular use across the organisation, and the KPI and KRA framework agreed and beginning to roll out.
* **Months 9 to 12:** 
 A first set of efficiency and cost findings delivered to leadership, with agreed actions, and clearer visibility between departments and leadership than the institution has today.



**Who this role suits, and who it does not** 



* This role will suit someone who takes satisfaction in making systems and people work well together, and who is willing to be the person who asks why a process exists at all. It involves sustained work across departments, some of it against resistance, and it rewards patience, follow\-through and clear judgement more than technical brilliance alone.
* It will not suit someone looking to build software products, lead a large engineering team, or work primarily in code. It will also not suit someone who is strong on analysis but light on the human and organisational side, because that human and organisational side is the larger part of the job. iLEAD is an education institution, not a software company. The work here is a better\-run, more efficient organisation.



**How to apply** 




 Please send your CV and a short note on a system, tool or measurement you introduced somewhere, and how you got people to actually use it, to
 **recruitment@ilead.net.in**

title: Marketplace Manager
description:
We're looking for a Marketplace Manager to own Eyemode's presence and performance on Amazon and Myntra. You'll be responsible for everything from listing quality and catalog health to advertising, pricing, inventory coordination, and P\&L for each platform. This is a high\-ownership, hands\-on role for someone who wants to build a marketplace function from the ground up at a fast\-growing brand.
 



  





 Key Responsibilities
 



**Platform Operations \& Onboarding** 



* Own end\-to\-end account management across Amazon Seller/Vendor Central and Myntra
* Lead onboarding onto new categories/sub\-brands within these platforms, including approvals and catalog setup
* Manage day\-to\-day operations: order processing, returns/RTO management, claims, and platform compliance



**Catalog \& Listing Quality** 



* Create and optimize product listings (titles, bullet points, descriptions, backend keywords, A\+ content) tailored to each platform's algorithm and audience
* Ensure all material and product claims are accurate and verifiable — no unverified claims on frame materials (metal, acetate, cellulose propionate, etc.)
* Maintain catalog hygiene: correct categorization, images, sizing, and variant mapping
* Coordinate with the design/content team on marketplace\-specific creative assets



**Pricing, Promotions \& Revenue** 



* Set and manage pricing strategy across both platforms, balancing MRP integrity, platform\-specific margins, and competitiveness
* Plan and execute participation in platform sale events (Amazon Great Indian Festival, Myntra EORS, etc.)
* Manage advertising spend on Amazon Ads and Myntra Ads, optimizing for ROAS/ACOS
* Track and improve conversion rate, CTR, and organic ranking per SKU on each platform



  





  





 What We're Looking For
 


* 1\-2 years of experience in marketplace/e\-commerce management, ideally in fashion, lifestyle, D2C, or eyewear

title: Senior Product Analyst
description:
hoichoi is India's leading Bengali OTT platform — the digital arm of SVF, Eastern India's largest media \& entertainment company. We stream 650\+ Bengali movies, 185\+ originals, and 3000\+ hours of content to a global audience of \~250 million Bengalis across India, Bangladesh, and 100\+ countries. We're part of a wider ecosystem alongside Sooper (AI\-led micro\-drama OTT) and LoglineAI (AI\-native creative studio), and we're on a mission to entertain everyone in their native language.
 



  





**The Opportunity** 




 We're hiring a Senior Product Analyst to become the first dedicated owner of product analytics at hoichoi. We've been running PostHog for a few months, with real event data flowing across all platforms — what's missing is someone who digs into the data unprompted and turns it into a clear case for what we should change, and why. You'll sit inside the Product \& Data team and work closely with Engineering, Payments, and Programming to move two numbers: revenue and user experience.
 



  





 This is not a reporting service desk. As the first dedicated hire in this function, you will define how it works rather than inherit it. Your output is decisions, not dashboards — finding the exact step where a subscriber drops off, and owning a recommendation through to whether the number actually moved. We want someone who's done this before, checks the data before forming a view, and is comfortable reporting a flat result honestly. This is a full\-time, in\-office role based in Kolkata.
 



  





**What You'll Do**




  





**Drop\-off Analysis** 



* Map every meaningful journey on every platform and find the exact step where users leave: onboarding, login and signup, search, content discovery, playback start, and the subscription funnel.
* Own the subscription funnel end to end — app open → paywall viewed → plan selected → payment initiated → payment success — split by platform, geography, and payment method.
* For every drop\-off found, report how many users and how much revenue it costs, why it's happening, and what specifically should change.
* Analyse payment failures and retry behaviour alongside the payments team.
* Track whether each recommended fix moved the number, and report plainly if it didn't.



**Retention, Churn \& Cohorts** 



* Build and maintain retention and cohort views — day\-1/7/30, trial\-to\-paid, renewal, and cancellation.
* Identify first\-session and first\-week behaviours that predict a subscriber sticking around, and recommend how to engineer more of them.



**Content \& Programming Analytics** 



* Report on content performance — tray impressions and clicks, play starts, completion rates, drop\-off curves, and search behaviour.
* Feed insights back to the programming team on what to promote, tray order, and whether an underperforming release was a content or merchandising issue.
* Support the internal Programming Analyst tooling built on top of PostHog.



**Experimentation** 



* Set up and read A/B tests and feature\-flag rollouts in PostHog — paywall variants, onboarding flows, tray layouts.
* Define success metrics and guardrail metrics up front, and call results honestly, including flat ones.



**Reporting Rhythm** 



* Run a weekly product metrics review that people actually read, and a monthly deep dive on one problem area of your choosing.
* Deliver release\-impact analysis after every major app release.



  





**Must\-Have Qualifications :** 



* 4–6 years in product analytics, growth analytics, or data analysis on a consumer (B2C) product — app or web — including experience mentoring or setting standards for others.
* Hands\-on ownership of a product analytics tool (PostHog, Mixpanel, Amplitude, CleverTap, or similar) — has defined events, built funnels, and debugged bad data, not just consumed dashboards someone else built.
* Demonstrated ability to find drop\-offs and act on them, with a concrete example of a funnel fixed, what was found, what changed, and what it was worth.
* Solid grasp of funnels, cohorts, retention curves, and segmentation.
* Comfortable working with AI tooling day to day — specifically the PostHog MCP server with Claude — and able to get MCP running within a week if new to it.
* Willing to check the data and then take a decision: form a view, recommend it clearly, and own the outcome.
* Able to write a clear recommendation — what the data says, what to do about it, and how confident to be.
* Self\-directed, arriving with questions rather than waiting for answers.



  





  





**Candidates must have experience in any product analytics tool: PostHog, Mixpanel, Amplitude, CleverTap or similar.** 




  





**Why Join hoichoi** 




 You'll be the first dedicated product analytics hire at India's leading Bengali OTT platform — defining how the function works rather than inheriting someone else's playbook, with real event data across six platforms from day one. Every recommendation you make has a direct line to revenue and to how millions of viewers experience the product. hoichoi is going all\-in on becoming AI\-native, so you'll work daily with the PostHog MCP server and Claude as part of your core workflow, with a clear path to owning a growing analytics function as it scales.
 



  





**Culture \& How We Work** 




 At hoichoi, the best idea wins, not the biggest title. We operate in small, cross\-functional teams that argue productively and ship fast. Ownership isn't a buzzword here; it's the default setting — if something's broken, you fix it rather than filing a ticket and waiting.
 



  





 We ship fast, measure what works, and iterate. Some releases — particularly TV platform and store submissions — land outside standard hours, and we expect flexibility around those windows. We're equally serious about keeping the pace sustainable the rest of the time.
